name: Seafood beyond sushi and sashimi

origin.era: Salted salmon paid as tax from the late 7th century (farm ministry)

cells.what: Salted salmon, roe in the sac (sujiko) or loosened (ikura), and dishes that use the whole fish
cells.method: Dry-salting for large fish, brining for roe; soy-marinated ikura is common at home
cells.season: Autumn runs; harako-meshi around September to November
cells.know: The word ikura is said to come from Russian; how it arrived has more than one story

cells.what: Pufferfish, best known as thin-sliced sashimi with ponzu
cells.method: Only licensed handlers may prepare it; the liver may not be sold or served
cells.know: The toxin is not destroyed by cooking; licences differ by prefecture

origin.era: Anago-meshi sold as a station lunch from 1901

cells.what: Two long-bodied fish: conger eel (anago) and pike conger (hamo)
cells.method: Edomae anago is simmered and brushed with tsume; Miyajima anago is grilled over rice; hamo needs honekiri, cutting the small bones
cells.season: Anago: traditionally late spring to summer; hamo: early summer to autumn
cells.know: Kyoto’s hamo mostly comes from the Seto Inland Sea and Genkai Sea

cells.what: Fish dried whole or after removing guts and gills, to keep it
cells.method: Sun-dried, salted then dried, boiled then dried, or grilled then dried
cells.season: Year-round; salmon toba is made when it is below 10°C
cells.know: Most are split from the belly; Odawara-biraki keeps the head and splits from the back

cells.what: Fish ground with salt and set by heat: kamaboko, chikuwa, hanpen and more
cells.know: Each region has its own: sasa-kamaboko in Miyagi, steamed board kamaboko in Odawara, jakoten in Ehime

cells.what: Kelp, mostly from Hokkaido, used for stock and simmered dishes
cells.method: Dried; wiped rather than washed before making stock
cells.know: Grown in the north, but eaten most distinctively in Osaka and Okinawa

lineages.name: Nori, wakame and mozuku
lineages.nameJa: 海苔・わかめ・もずく

cells.what: Farmed seaweeds: sheet nori, salted wakame, mozuku
cells.method: Nori is farmed on nets; wakame is blanched and salted
cells.season: New nori from early November; wakame March to April; mozuku harvest around April
cells.know: Over 95% of mozuku was from Okinawa in a 2007 prefectural report
